content.text:
Silhouette: Horizontal lion frame carried on two hind legs, golden eagle wings in place of the forelegs. Host frame: the lion sets the outline, body size, and overall frame. A single creature that combines a lion and a golden eagle. Head of the lion, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: behavior follows lion head/brain donor; body is lion torso and frame; eagle contributes only surface graft regions; golden eagle feathers in a few large patches over the forequarters and neck, at full strength with clean edges, color and surface unchanged inside each patch; lion coat everywhere else; ears are lion rounded ears; face is lion muzzle and eyes; feet are lion paws; head is fully lion head tissue; limbs are four lion legs; no forelimb-to-wing substitution, avoids six-limb mythic plan; lion mane in place of the mane; mane gated off: neck carries eagle feathers so mane hair has no haired substrate to show; skull is lion skull; tail is lion tail with tuft, fully lion tissue; golden eagle wings in place of the forelegs, standing on two hind legs; wings held for display or gliding, not powered flight. Pattern lines and texture flow follow the body outline. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): more patterned, irregular coat markings for a closed habitat. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing lion-eagle hybrid**
I'm planning a single creature with a lion's head and torso on two hind legs, swapping the forelegs for golden eagle wings, and adding large feather patches over the forequarters in a silhouette that still reads like a natural history illustration.
**Composing natural history illustration**
I'm drafting a side three-quarter, bipedal lion with golden eagle wings replacing the forelegs, standing on two hind legs, with lion coat, mane, and feather patches, set on a plain light background in a scientific illustration style.
**Refining lion illustration**
I'm adjusting the design to show a two-legged lion with no forelimbs, removing the leopard spots and extra limbs from the previous version.
